answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake that is costly to split, like a basalt foundation that cannot be faked by copying an identity. New agents start with willow-thin trust: small limits that only grow through a history of useful, attested work. Meanwhile, reputation travels like a sparrow carrying messages between services - verifiable attestations from independent peers - so one operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities still arrives with no history, no stake, and no one willing to vouch for them.
